claims: n262/n262_exact.json and n295/n295_exact.json state 262 and 295 unit squares as centre and unit edge direction rows of exact rationals, with the sides 166996934419035177/10000000000000000 and 35399386883430443/2000000000000000; #1007 and the root README round them up at 12 places as 16.699693441904 and 17.699693441716, and the folders' READMEs print 16.6996934419035177000000000 and 17.6996934417152215000000000, rounded up at 25 places. n262/n262_witness.yaml and n295/n295_witness.yaml state the same packings as packing.squares:Witness/v2 documents of rational corners. #1007 names the record's values at jlevy/squares f9ddfeeef, 16.70710678118655 (16 + sqrt(2)/2) at 262 and 17.70423279073603036 ((22 + 22 sqrt(2))/3) at 295, and the gains on them, 0.00741 and 0.00454, and says later commits leave these files unchanged.

The folders' READMEs and #1007 say each packing has a band of 72 squares, tilted by 25 to 30 degrees and arranged 4 squares wide and 18 long, along the diagonal, built from a closed-form layout, and axis-aligned squares in the two regions beside it, 190 at 262 and 223 at 295; an integer program placed the axis-aligned squares, a numerical optimization followed, and the result was rounded to exact rational coordinates; no coordinates of other packings were used. They say the packing for n = 295 is the packing for n = 262 with an L-shaped border of 33 axis-aligned squares, so its side is larger by exactly 1. They say no local optimality test was run, that the packings show small gaps, so a further small reduction of the sides is likely possible, and that no local or global optimality is proved. #1007 asks that the bounds be credited to Joost de Winter, Delft University of Technology.

verify_exact.py (separating axes) and check_area.py (the area of each close pair's clipped intersection), both Python's fractions.Fraction and its standard library only, are each folder's two exact checkers; #1007 says they report 558 close pairs at 262 and 626 at 295, that this repository's check_rational_witness_independent.py reports 'VERIFIED: 262 squares, 34191 pairs' and 'VERIFIED: 295 squares, 43365 pairs' on the witnesses, that both witness files validate against this repository's witness.schema.yaml with 0 errors, and that a further exact checker, written separately, compared each side with the irrational record side in exact arithmetic (2(s - 16)^2 < 1 at 262, (3s - 22)^2 < 968 at 295). #1007 says the construction, the search and the rational certificates were produced with Gemini Carbon (Google), and the conversion to the witness format and the checks were run with Claude (Anthropic), both under his direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
